content.value_statement: Incorrect structured data can prevent rich result eligibility and create search console errors. This skill creates accurate JSON-LD and guides validation for common page types.
actual_capabilities: Selects relevant schema.org types for organization, article, product, FAQ, event, local business, and breadcrumb pages.
Produces complete JSON-LD markup with required and recommended properties.
Combines related entities in an @graph structure.
Reviews existing structured data for missing fields, invalid values, and content mismatches.
Explains implementation patterns for static sites, React, Next.js, CMS platforms, and WordPress.
Provides validation and Search Console troubleshooting checklists.
limitations: It cannot guarantee that Google will display a rich result.
It needs accurate page content, URLs, images, dates, prices, and organization details from the user.
It does not replace a complete technical SEO audit.
Generated markup still requires validation and deployment in the target site.

use_cases.title: Launch Product Structured Data
use_cases.description: Create Product, Offer, rating, and breadcrumb markup that matches an ecommerce product page.

use_cases.title: Standardize Article Templates
use_cases.description: Build reusable Article and BreadcrumbList templates with dynamic CMS fields.

use_cases.title: Resolve Rich Result Errors
use_cases.description: Review existing markup and prioritize syntax, nesting, required property, and visible-content issues.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Organization Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Organization JSON-LD for [company name] at [website URL]. Include the logo, description, contact details, and these social profiles: [links].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a company homepage

prompt_templates.title: Add Article Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Create reusable Article and BreadcrumbList schema for our [CMS] blog template. Use these dynamic fields: [field list]. Identify any missing required data.

prompt_templates.title: Review Product Markup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing Product schema for this page content: [content]. Check offers, availability, ratings, reviews, URLs, and visible-content consistency. Provide corrected markup.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Connected Schema Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an @graph for [page URL] connecting Organization, WebSite, WebPage, BreadcrumbList, and [primary entity]. Define stable identifiers and explain each relationship.

output_examples.input: Add structured data to a SaaS homepage.
output: Recommended entities: Organization, WebSite, and SoftwareApplication.
A connected graph links the publisher, website, page, and software entity.
The implementation checklist covers required business details and validation.

output_examples.input: Why is valid product markup not producing rich results?
output_examples.output: The review separates syntax validity from eligibility and display. It checks visible content, required offer details, Search Console reports, and Google guidelines.

output_examples.input: Create a reusable blog schema template.
output_examples.output: The result maps CMS fields to article, author, publisher, image, publication date, modification date, and breadcrumb properties.

best_practices: Match every structured-data claim to content visible on the page.
Use fully qualified URLs, ISO 8601 dates, and supported enumeration values.
Validate before deployment and monitor Search Console after release.
anti_patterns: Do not add ratings, reviews, prices, or FAQs that users cannot see on the page.
Do not assume valid markup guarantees that a search engine will show rich results.
Do not duplicate conflicting schema entities from plugins, themes, and custom templates.

faq.question: What format does this skill recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends JSON-LD because it is easier to implement, maintain, and connect across multiple schema entities.

faq.question: Which schema types can it create?
faq.answer: It covers Organization, WebSite, Article, Product, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, HowTo, BreadcrumbList, LocalBusiness, Event, and connected graphs.

faq.question: Can it guarantee rich results?
faq.answer: No. Valid and eligible markup does not guarantee display because search engines decide when rich results appear.

faq.question: Can it fix existing schema errors?
faq.answer: It can review supplied markup and page content for syntax, nesting, required properties, invalid values, and content mismatches.

faq.question: Does it support dynamic websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides implementation guidance for React, Next.js, CMS templates, WordPress, and other server-rendered or static systems.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the page type, visible content, target rich results, existing markup, available data fields, URLs, and technical stack.
